title: Effect of Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Lumbar Active Discopathy
official: Effect of Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Lumbar Active Discopathy
summary:
Chronic low back pain, defined as pain in the lumbar region persisting for more than three months, is the leading cause of disability worldwide. A specific form of low back pain, characterized by vertebral endplate changes (known as Modic type 1 changes) and prolonged inflammatory pain, affects a subset of the population and is associated with active discopathy.

Current treatments are generally invasive and have limited efficacy (e.g., intradiscal injections, bracing). Auricular vagus nerve stimulation using electrical impulses delivered through an earbud-like device, such as Vagustim, is an innovative, clinically recognized, approved, and effective approach to restoring balance in parasympathetic nervous system dysfunction. However, no randomized controlled trial has yet evaluated its efficacy in chronic low back pain.

The aim of this study is therefore to conduct a comparative trial of auricular vagus nerve stimulation (experimental treatment) versus sham treatment, with the objective of improving pain management in chronic low back pain through a novel, non-invasive, and easy-to-use therapeutic approach.

We hypothesize that auricular vagus nerve stimulation has a clinically significant effect on low back pain intensity in patients with active discopathy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient with daily LBP for at least 3 months.
* Patient with mean LBP intensity ≥ 50 on VAS in the previous 48 hours.
* Lumbar Modic 1 changes on MRI for less than 6 months (defined as vertebral endplate subchondral bone hypointense signal in T1-weighted sequence and hyperintense signal in T2-weighted sequence, adjacent to degenerative disc disease), evaluated in the sagittal plane.
* Aged 18 to 65 years old.
* For reproductive aged woman: Negative pregnancy test at the time of inclusion and use of effective contraceptive during the entire period of exposure to the device, from Day 0 to Month 3. The following are accepted, amongst others: hormonal contraceptives (oral, transdermal, vaginal ring, injectable or implant), intrauterine devices, permanent contraceptive methods, as well as barrier methods, in particular male or female condoms, provided they are used correctly and consistently. The contraceptive method will be tailored to each participant's circumstances.
* Patient has agreed to take part in the study.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient with a history of back surgery (disk herniation, decompression, fusion and prosthesis).
* Pregnant patient.
* Patient under corticosteroid or strong opioids treatments during the last month.
* Patient with acute or chronic inflammatory disease.
* Patient with uncontrolled psychiatric condition.
* Patient with uncontrolled cardiovascular disease or with cardiac stimulation.
* Patient with a left cochlear implant.
* Patient with skin lesion and/or external otitis of the left ear.
* Patient being involved or having been involved in the 3 months previous to the inclusion visit, in an interventional research (RIPH type 1 or drug research or clinical investigation of MD).
* Patient under safeguard of justice, guardianship or curatorship.
* Patients under 18 years of age.
* Patients who are unable to provide feedback on the sensation of stimulation (intensity).
* Individuals with an active implantable device or any other implanted electronic or electrical device (pacemaker, defibrillator, etc.).
* Individuals prone to dermatological problems in the stimulation area.
* Individuals suffering from venous or arterial thrombosis, or thrombophlebitis.
* Individuals with a history of epilepsy.

Additional contraindications for vagal neurostimulation:

* Confirmed cardiac conditions
* Atrial conditions.
